official.deadline_note: Deadline of the published 2026/27 round: applications opened Monday 27 April 2026 and closed Friday 5 June 2026, a six-week window. That round is now closed and no 2027/28 window has been advertised on the portal as of 10 October 2026, so this is the most recent published deadline rather than an open one.
official.status_note: The 2026/27 In-Country Scholarship Scheme (ISS) application window is stated on the PTDF portal to run from Monday 27th April 2026 to Friday 5th June 2026 and has passed. The portal still hosts the 2026/27 guidelines and sponsored-course list, and PTDF publishes this scheme on an annual cycle (2021/22, 2023/24 and 2026/27 rounds are on record), so the next round is expected but is not yet announced.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published ISS guidelines do not state what the scholarship award pays for. No tuition, fee, stipend, book or living-allowance wording is published for the In-Country scheme; the separate Overseas Scholarship Scheme (OSS) notice does itemise benefits, and that wording has not been carried over to ISS.
eligibility: Applications are invited from interested and qualified Nigerians for the 2026/27 Undergraduate, Master's and PhD scholarships in Nigerian public universities only.
Applicants must have a National Identity Number (NIN) and verify it before proceeding with the application (NIMC verification charges apply).
Applicants who have benefited from any PTDF scholarship in the past cannot apply for the same or a lower category of degree, and current beneficiaries of any other scholarship need not apply.
Undergraduate applicants must be full-time students in a public university, presently at 200 level, having completed first-year examinations, with a minimum CGPA of 2.4 on a scale of 5.0.

Postgraduate applicants must hold a full-time admission letter into a public university, a minimum of Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field, at least 5 WAEC/SSCE/NECO credits including English Language and Mathematics, an NYSC certificate or letter of exemption, and a certificate of indigeneship; PhD applicants additionally need a minimum of Merit in a second-degree certificate.

The course of study must be related to the oil and gas, energy and management fields as advertised on the published list of sponsored courses; for PhD applicants the research area must be relevant to the oil and gas industry.
Admission for part-time studies shall not be considered for all categories of applications, and postgraduate applicants presently in their final year of studies need not apply.
requirements: Apply online through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng, after reading through the requirements.
Verify your NIN before starting the application; NIMC verification charges apply and a failed verification must be recovered through the portal's failed-verification route rather than paid for again.
Upload all documents as legible scans in PDF format, at the file sizes indicated in the portal, except the passport photograph.

Undergraduate uploads: WAEC/SSCE/NECO result with at least 5 credits including English Language and Mathematics (not more than 2 sittings, first sitting result uploaded), letter of admission, first-year academic transcript signed and stamped by the HOD/Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel, certificate of indigeneship, and a personal statement of a minimum of 300 words.

MSc applicants must submit a personal statement of at least 1,000 words stating the reasons for the study, its relevance to the industry and its expected impact on national development, plus a first-degree certificate or statement of results and an NYSC certificate or exemption letter.
PhD applicants must submit a research proposal of not more than 6 pages (template downloaded from the applicant's profile on the portal) plus a second-degree certificate or statement of results.
Postgraduate applicants who meet the requirements are shortlisted and invited to oral interviews before final selection.
documents: National Identity Number (NIN), verified before applying (NIMC verification charges apply)

WAEC/SSCE/NECO result(s) showing at least 5 credits including English Language and Mathematics, not more than 2 sittings; for undergraduates the first-sitting result is uploaded, and for postgraduates both results must precede the first degree
Letter of admission into the university (mandatory for undergraduate applicants; full-time admission for postgraduates)
First-year academic transcript signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel (undergraduates)
Certificate of indigeneship, evidencing state of origin and local government (all applicants)
Personal statement: minimum 300 words for undergraduates, minimum 1,000 words for MSc applicants
First-degree certificate or statement of results (postgraduates)
NYSC certificate or letter of exemption (postgraduates)
Second-degree certificate or statement of results (PhD applicants)
PhD research proposal of not more than 6 pages, using the template accessible via the applicant's profile on the portal
selection_criteria: Academic merit as evidenced by quality of degrees, full academic transcripts, other professional qualifications acquired, and relevant publications to be referenced by applicants
Viability of the study/research plan (PhD applicants only)
The statement of purpose for undergraduate and MSc applicants, making the case for the scholarship, the relevance of the study to the industry and its expected impact on national development

The research proposal for PhD applicants, covering topic, introduction, literature review, research question(s), methodology, mode of data collection, expected outcome(s), novelty, relevance to the industry and appropriate references
Grades on the transcript for undergraduate applicants, where transcripts must be signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or any authorised personnel of the university
Equitable representation of the 36 States of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory, except where a State does not have the requisite number of candidates to fill allotted slots
application_method: Visit scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng and create an applicant account, following the login and password instructions emailed to you.

Click Verify NIN before starting a new application and complete the verification (charges may apply); if a verification fails, use the portal's failed-verification route with your payment transaction reference and NIN instead of paying again.
Read and accept the terms and conditions/disclaimer to continue with the application.
Complete every field of the application form, observing the stated file formats and upload sizes, since an upload that does not meet the requirement produces an error.
Download the PhD proposal template from your applicant profile if applying under the PhD scheme, and upload the completed proposal with the other PDF documents.
Submit online; shortlisted postgraduate applicants are then invited to oral interviews before final selection.
official.application_route: Online only, through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng: create an applicant account, verify your NIN, accept the disclaimer, complete the form and upload PDF documents; there is no paper route.
official.study_mode: Full-time only; admission for part-time studies is not considered in any category
official.citizenship_residency: Nigerian citizens; application is restricted to Nigerian public universities, with selection weighted toward equitable representation of the 36 states and the FCT
official.international_eligibility: No. The scheme invites applications from qualified Nigerians only and is restricted to Nigerian public universities.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The course must appear on the published list of sponsored courses and be related to the oil and gas, energy and management fields as advertised (engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management courses); for PhD applicants the research area must be relevant to the oil and gas industry.
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants must submit a research proposal of not more than 6 pages covering topic, introduction, literature review, research question(s), methodology, mode of data collection, expected outcome(s), novelty, relevance to the industry and appropriate references, using the template downloaded from the applicant's profile on the portal.
official.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund, a Federal Government of Nigeria agency mandated to develop indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology to meet the needs of the oil and gas industry, invites applications from qualified Nigerians for the 2026/27 Undergraduate, Master's and PhD scholarships in Nigerian public universities only, on a published list of sponsored courses related to oil and gas, energy and management. The scheme is described as highly competitive and merit-driven, with selection weighted toward equitable representation of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
official.region: Nigeria - national scheme drawing applicants from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory
official.program_type: In-Country Scholarship Scheme (ISS) - federal government agency scholarship for undergraduate and postgraduate study

verification.notes: Guidelines, sponsored-course list, approved ISS university list and the portal how-to-apply steps were read directly on scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng. PTDF publishes no award value and no itemisation of what the ISS award pays for; the benefit wording published for the separate Overseas Scholarship Scheme was deliberately not carried across, and the amount fields are therefore null.

applicant_utility.summary: PTDF's In-Country Scholarship Scheme sends Nigerians to study full-time at Nigerian public universities only, and the 2026/27 round closed on 5 June 2026 after a six-week window that opened on 27 April 2026. What the award actually pays is not published anywhere on the fund's portal, so treat the value as unknown rather than assuming it covers tuition and upkeep. Your leverage is in the hard gates instead: a verified NIN, a course that is exactly on the sponsored list, a full-time admission letter, and an indigeneship certificate. Since the scheme recurs annually, expect the next window around April-June 2027 and use the gap to get transcripts stamped and a 1,000-word MSc statement or a 6-page PhD proposal drafted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nigerian undergraduates at 200 level in a sponsored engineering, science, environmental, renewable-energy or management course at a public university, and MSc/PhD applicants with a 2:2 or better in an oil and gas-related field who already hold a full-time admission letter.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your NIN as the first task, keep the payment reference, and if the NIMC verification fails use the portal's failed-verification route with that reference instead of paying again; NIN problems go to iss.applications@ptdf.gov.ng.
Match your exact course title against the published sponsored-course list and confirm your university appears on the approved ISS schools list before you invest time in the form.
Undergraduates: request your first-year transcript now and get it signed and stamped by the HOD or Exams Officer; postgraduates: request full academic transcripts from your registry in advance.
Obtain a certificate of indigeneship from your local government and, for postgraduates, your NYSC discharge certificate or exemption letter.
Draft the MSc personal statement to at least 1,000 words and the PhD proposal to no more than 6 pages, then transfer it into the template downloaded from your portal profile.
Scan every document as a legible PDF inside the file-size limits shown by the portal, leaving only the passport photograph as an image.
common_rejection_risks: A course that is not on the sponsored list, or only loosely related to oil and gas, energy or management.
Illegible or falsified documents, and uploads that breach the portal's file-size limits.
Part-time admission in any category, which is explicitly not considered.
Being a former PTDF beneficiary at the same or a lower degree category, or currently holding any other scholarship.
Weak first-year grades, because undergraduate selection is decided on transcript results.
Losing a state quota slot: selection is distributed across the 36 states and the FCT, so a strong file from an over-represented state can still miss out.
document_audit: Upload the first-sitting WAEC/SSCE/NECO result only, and keep within the two-sitting limit; for postgraduates both sittings must precede the first degree.
The current guidelines set no validity window on admission letters (the 2021/22 advert required postgraduate admission within 12 months), so use a recent admission letter rather than an old one.
An unstamped or unsigned first-year transcript is a standard fail point for undergraduates; the stamp must come from the HOD, Exams Officer or another authorised officer.
The PhD proposal must be written inside the portal template and kept to six pages; a longer or differently formatted proposal is a needless risk.
The certificate of indigeneship must show both state of origin and local government, not just one of them.
The passport photograph is the only upload that is not a PDF; everything else, including the personal statement and proposal, must be PDF.
alerts: The 2026/27 window closed on 5 June 2026 and no 2027/28 round has been announced as of 10 October 2026, so watch the portal news page rather than assuming a fixed calendar.
NIN verification is a paid step and the portal has carried NIMC server-maintenance notices; verify early in the window and never pay twice for the same NIN.
Postgraduate shortlisting and interview invitations are communicated by email, so use an email address you check regularly and keep the phone numbers on the portal live.
Postgraduate applicants in their final year of study are excluded, as are holders of any other current scholarship - check these two rules before spending money on NIN verification.

Support is only available weekdays: live chat 9am-5pm and phone/WhatsApp 8:30am-4:30pm on +234 809 250 0006/0007 and WhatsApp +234 809 250 0008, so do not leave a portal problem to the final day of the window.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an applicant account on the portal, verify your NIN (paid, once), accept the disclaimer, complete every field and upload the PDFs, then submit online; shortlisted postgraduates are emailed for an oral interview before the final award list is released.
